rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here misery means worldly toil from expulsion, not ultimate misery: if that were intended, Adam could not later have entered the Garden, and the clause after fa is a predicate that cannot fail.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو أرادها ما دخل الجنة بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exile would remove the four supports of human sufficiency: satiety, drink, clothing, and shelter.
rows.anchor: من الأقطاب التي يدور علها كفاف الإنسان , وهي الشبع والري والكسوة والكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names the opposites of these blessings by negation so Adam hears the kinds of misery he was warned against and recoils from their cause, while learning that caution cannot defeat destiny.
rows.anchor: بافظ النفي لنقائضها ليطرق سمعه بأسماء أصناف الشقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains لك as a benefit incumbent upon God to grant: Adam will never go hungry or be stripped, inwardly or outwardly.
rows.anchor: فلا يتجرد باطنك ولا ظاهرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thirst is an inner burning, while exposure is being struck by the sun's heat; neither inward nor outward heat will afflict Adam there.
rows.anchor: أي لا يكون بحيث يصيبك حر الشمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's whisper followed the warning without a temporal gap.
rows.anchor: تحذيرنا هذا من غير بعد في الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whisperer is the expelled Iblis, who insinuated hidden suggestions into Adam's heart through the access God allowed him among this kind.
rows.anchor: أي ألقى إليه وجه الخفاء بما مكناه من الجري في هذا النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ila highlights how readily humans accept contrary suggestions even when they arrive later; alternatively, the whisper reached Adam through his wife, hence lam when both spouses are mentioned.
rows.anchor: لأن المقام لبيان سرعة قبول هذا النوع للنقائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan first whets the desire to know by offering guidance, then promises a tree of immortality and an imperishable kingdom, exploiting the human love of long life.
rows.anchor: فإن النفس شديدة الطلب لعلم ما تجهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan presents the forbidden tree as the sole barrier between Adam and permanent dominion, calling it a kingdom that never decays.
rows.anchor: بينك وبين الملك الدائم غلا أن تأكل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and his wife ate after forgetting the covenant; their nakedness appeared as they broke the prohibition's covering, so they began sewing or sticking Garden leaves over themselves.
rows.anchor: متعين لقوله ناسيين ما عهد إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even though Adam forgot, his high rank required extra care, constant watchfulness, firm resolve, and alert thought in observing the prohibition.
rows.anchor: لأن عظم مقامه وعلو رتبته يقتضيان له مزيد الاعتناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Adam's Lord recalls the benefactions by which He honored him beyond his descendants: shaping him by hand, commanding the angels to prostrate, and opposing his enemy.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليه بما لم ينله أحدا من بنيه من تصويره له بيده وإسجاد ملائكته له ومعاداة من عاداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawa means straying from the sound path: Adam wrongly sought immortality by disobeying his Lord, yet this did not remove him from the rank of divine election.
rows.anchor: فأخطأ طريق التوصل إلى الخلد بمخالفة أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the apparent distance between Adam's quick obedience to the enemy and God's later favor, God chose him, accepted his repentance as a return to right guidance, and preserved him as one near to Him.
rows.anchor: أثبت ذلك تعالى مشيرا إليه بأداة التراخي فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent answers the listener's curiosity after Adam's wife and Iblis were mentioned without the rest of their story; the holy royal abode cannot contain such disobedience, though God had prepared Adam for it through election.
rows.anchor: لم تسكن عن تشوفها إلى سماع بقية الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties addressed are Adam and those who follow him, together with Iblis.
rows.anchor: أيها الفريقان : آدم وتبعه , وإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enmity between the camps stirs resolve after forgetfulness and weakened determination: the jinn mislead humans, humans guard against them with charms and incantations, and members of each camp also oppose one another.
rows.anchor: حرك العزم بعث الهم بإيقاع العداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence of enmity is that no one can guard against an enemy except through God; His guidance, conveyed through the Book and an intellectually supported Messenger, is the only protection.
rows.anchor: لا قدرة لأحد منكم على التحرز من عدوه إلا بي ولا حرز لكم من قبلي إلا اتباع أمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The morphology of ittabaʿa (form VIII) conveys effortful, complete following, prompted by the great importance of the guidance.
rows.anchor: التي فيها تكلف وتتميم للتبع الناشىء عن شدة الاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The follower of God's guidance will not stray from the right path in either life or suffer in any undertaking in either life.
rows.anchor: عن طريق السداد في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since misery is the penalty for error, denying misery also denies fear and grief, making this promise stronger than the one in al-Baqara; this context urges fearful striving against enmity and neglect.
rows.anchor: فإن الشقاء عقاب الضلال , ويلزم من نفيه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi in al-Lawami defines misery as the servant's separation from God and happiness as reaching Him.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : والشقاء : فراق العبد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani reports Ibn Abbas saying that God guarantees the Qur'an's follower will not stray in this world or be miserable in the next.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from remembrance is deliberate abandonment of what benefits a person; remembrance here means God's guidance.
rows.anchor: بتعمد الترك لما ينفعه بالمجاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form of maʿisha diminishes it, while ḍankan is an especially harsh verbal noun whose form is unchanged across gender and number.
rows.anchor: حقرها سبحانه بالتأنيث ثم وصفها بأفظع وصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life is constricted because misguidance inevitably ends in distress, even when outwardly spacious; the cause is named for its eventual effect, as greed, miserliness, rivalries, and worry leave no contentment or security.
rows.anchor: فهو ضنك لكونه سببا للضيق

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim says that if Adam's son had a valley of gold he would seek another, then a third, and only dust fills his belly; God accepts the repentance of the repentant.
rows.anchor: متفق عليه عن أنس رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, one wholly devoted to remembrance is content and satisfied; remembrance expands the breast and illuminates the heart, so inward meaning matters more than outward appearances.
rows.anchor: مستكثر ن ذكر الله الشارح للصدور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person rises from the grave seeing but becomes blind when driven to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إذا خرج من القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the nearer literal reading that blindness applies to some misguided people, which fits the statement that they will see clearly when they come to God.
rows.anchor: بعض أهل الضلال ليجتمع مع قوله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report from Ibn Umar quotes the Prophet saying that wrongdoing is layers of darkness on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing God as Lord recalls prior blessings to elicit mercy, since a benefactor tends to preserve a blessing while there remains room for the recipient's reform.
rows.anchor: أي أيها المحسن إلي المسبغ نعمه علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika may mean that the person acted shamefully in this way in life, or that matters were as he said; the reply then explains the first reading and gives the cause on the second.
rows.anchor: مثل هذا الفعل الشنيع فعلت في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God's signs means treating them with the neglect of something unseen, making oneself blind in sight and insight, as those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance.
rows.anchor: معاملة المنسي الذي لا يبصره صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today the person is left in blindness and the Fire's misery, like an object no one sees or attends to.
rows.anchor: تترك على ما أنت عليه بالعمى والشقاء بالنار

words: مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same severe recompense is given to one who exceeds bounds by following desire and arrogantly rejects God's commands, whether by denial or by acting like a denier.
rows.anchor: في متابعة هواه فتكبر عن متابعة أوامرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment of the Hereafter, in whatever form, is harsher and more lasting than worldly punishment because this world is transient and a place of departure.
rows.anchor: فإن الدنيا دار زوال , وموضع قلعة وارتحال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Majah reports from Ibn Masud that the person who makes the Hereafter the sole concern is spared worldly worry, whereas one whose concerns fragment across worldly affairs may perish in any valley without God's care.
rows.anchor: سمعت نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Majah reports from Zayd ibn Thabit that a worldly aim scatters one's affairs and leaves poverty before one's eyes, while an intention for the Hereafter gathers affairs and puts richness in the heart.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت رضي اله عنه : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting ancient peoples' stories, answering Jewish challenges, and interweaving wisdom and admonition with a call to piety, the sūrah marvels that Quraysh still refuse truth through pride or fear of consequences.
rows.anchor: ما ذكر من قصص الأولين وأخبار الماضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand a sign like those given to former peoples, from Muhammad, God's Messenger and beneficiary.
rows.anchor: أي محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's rulings and wisdom in unsurpassed meanings and arrangement already silence eloquent people and prove it is God's speech, though the opponents obstinately count none of these proofs as a sign.
rows.anchor: ما أعجز بلغاءهم , وأبكم فصحاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scriptures include the books of Abraham, Moses, Jesus, David, the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other divine books; the sūrah's accounts of Adam and Moses illustrate their contents.
rows.anchor: صحف إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى وداود عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an recounts prior-scriptural events accurately in a form unknown to all but a few experts, without studying with them and without anyone able to match its arrangement; this establishes God as its sole teacher and messenger.
rows.anchor: من غير أن يخالط عالما منهم أو من غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an itself witnesses to prior scriptures, as a proof bears witness for what is proved; it needs no witness and surpasses all the signs requested of earlier prophets by an immeasurable degree.
rows.anchor: لا افتقار له بعد العجز عنه إلى شيء أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had destroyed them before the Qur'an, they would claim on Judgment Day that no messenger had been sent to command obedience; the hypothetical acknowledges a plausible excuse after their baseless attack on the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ما كان لهم فيه نوع شبهة لو وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before it refers to the Qur'an just mentioned and nearby verses, including the command not to hasten the Qur'an and the sūrah's opening assurance that it was not sent to cause hardship.
rows.anchor: من قبل هذا القرآن المذكور في الآية الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Prophet and treated the people gently, lifting the rust from willing hearts with repeated reminders and signs until His command was affirmed, the Prophet's rank raised, and his followers increased and aided.
rows.anchor: ونحن نترفق بهم , ونكشف عن قلوب من شئنا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith is nearly impossible and their disputation will not end: they criticize guidance if it comes and protest if punishment comes, so the Prophet is told that both sides await the outcome.
rows.anchor: وجدالهم لا ينقطع , بل إن جاءهم الهدى طعنوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣirāṭ is a clear, broad road; sawiyy means straight, without a bend or rise, and fit to reach one's aims.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا عوج فيه ولا نتو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possessing something does not mean one knows or uses it, so the verse also asks who attained guidance, gained benefit, and avoided harm: the Prophet's side or theirs.
rows.anchor: قد لا يكون عالما بالشيء ولا عاملا بما يعلم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome became clear at the conquest of Mecca: they rejoiced greatly in Islam and entered it from hope in clemency and generosity and fear of the sword and punishment, later marveling at their earlier hesitation.
rows.anchor: ودخلوا رغبة في الحلم والكرم , ورهبة من السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his followers are the fortunate, content people in both lives; the end of the sūrah returns to its opening assurance that revelation was not sent to make the Prophet miserable, showing God's forbearance toward the exalted.
rows.anchor: هم السعداء الأغنياء الراضون في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After adducing the heavens and earth as signs of God's greatness, the sūrah detailed familiar earthly features and the region's many mountains, then turns to the sky.
rows.anchor: دلهم بالسموات والأرض على عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sky is used generically because most people observe only the lowest heaven, and because speaking of one protected roof conveys its preservation.
rows.anchor: وأفرادها بإرادة الجنس لأن أكثر الناس لا يشاهدون منها إلا الدنيا ولأن الحفظ للشيء الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is a roof over earth, but unlike familiar roofs it is filled with indispensable benefits, including light sources, guidance signs, and ornaments beyond reckoning.
rows.anchor: وهذه مشحونة بالمنافع فأكثر ما ينزل منها ما لا غنى للناس عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This roof is protected from falling by divine power and from devils by meteors.
rows.anchor: أي عن السقوط بالقدرة وعن الشياطين بالشهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people turn away from the sky's innumerable signs, including large and small stars, winds, and rains, which prove God's power over resurrection and His exclusive divinity and perfection.
rows.anchor: الدالة على قدرتنا على كل ما نريد من البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fail to contemplate the ordered management of the sky through risings, settings, and celestial arrangement, which indicates calculations governing benefits.
rows.anchor: لا يتفكرون فيما فيها من التسيير والتدبير بالمطالع والمغارب والترتيب القويم الدال على الحساب الدائر عليه سائر المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created night and day and their signs, the sun that gives rise to day and the moon that marks night; naming the greatest signs also implies the other stars.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبعهما آيتيهما فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the named celestial bodies each swim in the orbit appointed for them; the masculine rational plural pronoun is used by grammatical predominance.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد يسبح في الفلك الذي جعل به

words: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ ٱلْخُلْدَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since night and day wear down every life, God made no human before Muhammad immortal; the wording answers claims that earlier people were everlasting.
rows.anchor: من الليل والنهار , كان كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this one of the strongest proofs that al-Khidr died: long life is not immortality, as with Jesus, but the cited Prophetic reports indicate al-Khidr's death and leave no stronger evidence for survival.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أقوى الأدلة على أن الخضر عليه السلام مات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed at Badr that if this company were destroyed, no one would worship God on earth after that day, a report cited as evidence of al-Khidr's death.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( اللهم إن تهلك هذه العصابة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that within a hundred years none of those alive on earth at that time would remain, cited as evidence of al-Khidr's death.
rows.anchor: لا يبقى على رأس مائة سنة ممن هو على ظهر الأرض اليوم أحد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet wished Moses had been patient so that the account of Moses and al-Khidr could have been told further, another report in the argument that al-Khidr died.
rows.anchor: وددنا أن موسى عليه السالم صبر فقص علينا من أمرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters reasoned that they were the wrongdoers: they put worship in the wrong place, while Abraham was right to humiliate the idols and they had left their idols unguarded after worshipping them.
rows.anchor: بمعنى أنهم فكروا فيما قال فاضطرهم الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their acknowledgment identifies them as wrongdoers for worshipping what cannot speak or act and for leaving their idols without protection.
rows.anchor: لكونكم وضعتم العبادة في غير موضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukis means they immediately reversed themselves and returned from truth to error, as a sick person who relapses to an earlier state; the image turns their upper parts downward.
rows.anchor: أي انقلبوا في الحال غير مستحيين مما يلزمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argue that Abraham knows the idols, whole or broken, cannot speak; thinking this helps defend their partners, they instead give Abraham grounds for decisive arguments.
rows.anchor: فكانوا بما فاهوا به ظانين أنه ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham rebukes them for worshipping beneath God, the supreme sovereign who alone controls benefit and harm through His complete attributes.
rows.anchor: منكرا عليهم موبخا لهم مسببا عن إقرارهم

words: مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they urgently seek help after their idols were smashed, Abraham puts benefit first: the idols can neither provide what they hope for nor cause what they fear.
rows.anchor: بسبب تكسير أصنامهم , راجين من ينفعهم في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff expresses Abraham's disgust and contempt; the author directs the reader to recall a parallel passage in al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: أي تقذر وتحقير مني , وفي الأحقاف

words: لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His contempt is directed both at the idolaters and at what they worship, which lies far below every rank under God, the supreme King.
rows.anchor: كانت جميع الرتب تحت رتبته تعالى , وكانت أصنامهم هذه
